undici.reason: Downstream response desynchronization via the retry interceptor, affecting >=7.0.0 <=7.28.0, fixed 7.29.0. One of FIVE undici advisories fixed in that release — the others are cross-user information disclosure via degenerate private cache directives (GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272), CRLF injection via a blob-like body `type` (GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5), cross-user disclosure via whitespace around equals in Cache-Control (GHSA-jr45-8vmc-qm54), and cookie-attribute injection via unsanitized domain (GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm) — so one floor clears all five. undici is a direct production dependency. Floor 7.28.0 -> 7.29.0 on 2026-08-04: the previous floor, added for GHSA-vxpw-j846-p89q, was itself the top of this cluster's range. Held on 7.x — 8.x is a breaking major.

tar.reason: Three advisories on the 7.5.x line, each superseding the last: path-traversal on extraction (GHSA-8489-44mv-ggj8, fixed 7.5.16, added in #1252), CVE-2026-59871 / GHSA-w8wr-v893-vjvp (<=7.5.17, fixed 7.5.18), a CRITICAL at GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw (<=7.5.18, fixed 7.5.19), and GHSA-r292-9mhp-454m (<=7.5.20, fixed 7.5.21). Floor raised 7.5.18 → 7.5.21 on 2026-07-25: the previous floor was ITSELF inside the critical advisory range.
tar.currentlyInert: The ONLY tar in the tree is npm's bundled copy (node_modules/npm/node_modules/tar), reached via libnpmdiff / node-gyp / pacote. npm ships its dependencies bundled, so an override cannot rewrite them — what actually cleared CVE-2026-59871 was bumping the `npm` pin to ^11.18.0, whose bundle carries tar 7.5.19. Kept as a floor in case tar re-enters the real tree (the guard will then require this note to be removed), but it is protecting nothing today.

npm.reason: Dev-only, via @semantic-release/npm. npm ships its dependency tree BUNDLED and overrides cannot rewrite bundled deps, so raising this pin is the only lever on the copies inside it: 11.18.0 carries tar 7.5.19 (clearing CVE-2026-59871) and brace-expansion 5.0.7. Re-kinded bundle-vehicle on 2026-07-25 — it was recorded as a security override citing GHSA-4v6q-8jgv-6q2j, an id that resolves to nothing, because no npm-CLI advisory is fixed in 11.18.0. The justification is the bundle, not an advisory on npm itself. npm 12.x requires Node ^24.15 (we run 24.14), so 11.18 is the ceiling until the runtime moves.

picomatch.reason: ReDoS via extglob quantifiers on adversarial glob input, reached through the test/build matcher chain. The same 4.0.4 release fixes GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p (method injection in POSIX character classes), so one floor clears both. Was recorded as GHSA-2p57-rm9w-gvfp until 2026-07-25 — that id is an `ip` SSRF advisory and has nothing to do with picomatch.

protobufjs.reason: DoS via an infinite loop in .proto parsing, affecting >=8.0.0 <=8.6.5. Pulled by the OpenTelemetry OTLP exporter, which sits in the production tree. Floor raised 8.2.0 → 8.6.6 on 2026-07-25: the old floor targeted GHSA-jggg-4jg4-v7c6 (fixed 8.2.0) and had been superseded, so it admitted the still-vulnerable 8.6.5. The previously recorded GHSA-h755-8qp9-cq85 is real but patched at 6.11.4 / 7.2.5 — it never justified an 8.x floor.

@hono/node-server.currentlyInert: Left the tree entirely on 2026-08-03. It only ever arrived transitively via @prisma/dev, which pinned @hono/node-server 1.19.11; the prisma 7.8.0 → 7.9.1 bump moved @prisma/dev 0.24.3 → 0.24.17, which no longer depends on it. The override is KEPT rather than deleted so the 2.0.10 floor re-applies automatically if anything reintroduces the package — deleting it would silently drop that protection with no signal.
@hono/node-server.reason: Unauthenticated memory-leak DoS affecting >=2.0.0 <=2.0.9, fixed 2.0.10. Paired with the `hono` override. Floor raised 2.0.5 → 2.0.10 on 2026-07-25: the old floor cleared only the earlier serve-static path traversal (GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9, fixed 2.0.5) and admitted versions this later advisory still affects.

fast-uri.reason: Host confusion via a backslash authority introducer, affecting >=3.0.0 <=3.1.4, fixed 3.1.5, reached through the Ajv/schema-validation chain. Floor 3.1.4 -> 3.1.5 on 2026-08-04: the previous floor cleared only GHSA-v2hh-gcrm-f6hx and was itself the top of this newer advisory's range. Held on the 3.x line deliberately — 4.x is a breaking major and nothing here needs it.

hono.currentlyInert: Left the tree entirely on 2026-08-03, same cause as the paired @hono/node-server entry: hono only ever arrived via @prisma/dev (^4.12.8), and the prisma 7.8.0 → 7.9.1 bump moved @prisma/dev 0.24.3 → 0.24.17, which dropped the dependency. Override KEPT rather than deleted so the 4.12.27 floor re-applies automatically if hono returns.
hono.reason: Server-side XSS via a JSX escaping bypass in cx() (fixed 4.12.27), one of a cluster of hono advisories fixed in that release. THE cautionary entry: pinned ^4.12.23 while the lockfile sat on vulnerable 4.12.25 — the range permitted the fix but nothing pulled it in. Raising a floor is not enough; the lockfile has to move too. Was recorded as GHSA-hcxr-2v8p-3vqw until 2026-07-25 — that id does not resolve as an npm advisory.

tmp.reason: Path traversal via a type-confusion bypass of `_assertPath`, affecting >=0.2.6 <0.2.7. Reached through build/test tooling. Floor raised 0.2.6 → 0.2.7 on 2026-07-25: the old floor cleared the EARLIER traversal (GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65, unsanitized prefix/postfix, fixed 0.2.6) but admitted 0.2.6 itself, which the follow-up advisory affects. The previously recorded GHSA-52f5-9888-68mp does not exist — the real low-severity arbitrary-write entry is GHSA-52f5-9888-hmc6, fixed back in 0.2.4.

@grpc/grpc-js.reason: A malformed request crashes the server; the 1.14.x line is fixed in 1.14.4. Pulled by the OpenTelemetry gRPC exporter in the production tree. The same release fixes GHSA-99f4-grh7-6pcq (malformed compressed message). Was recorded as GHSA-7v5v-9h63-cj86 until 2026-07-25 — real, but patched at 1.8.22 / 1.9.15 / 1.10.9, so it never justified a 1.14.4 floor.

uuid.reason: Missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when `buf` is provided. next-auth@4 declares uuid@^8.3.2 and the whole <11.1.1 line is affected, so forcing the patched major is the only fix. next-auth uses the version-stable named exports (v4, …), unchanged v8 → v11.

brace-expansion.reason: DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays that BYPASSES the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation (<=5.0.8, fixed 5.0.9) — the previous 5.0.8 floor, added for GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, was itself inside the new advisory's range. Floor 5.0.8 -> 5.0.9 on 2026-08-04. The KEY also had to change, from `brace-expansion@>=3.0.0 <=5.0.6` to `brace-expansion@>=5.0.0 <5.0.9`, and the reason is worth knowing: an npm override key carrying a version selector is matched against the declared SPECIFIER, not the resolved version, and a window spanning several majors (>=3.0.0) stopped matching the 5.x parents entirely — the top-level instance sat on vulnerable 5.0.8 through a full lockfile refresh with no error, the override silently biting nothing. Verified empirically: `>=3.0.0 <=5.0.8` left 5.0.8 in place; `>=5.0.0 <5.0.9` pulls 5.0.9. Keeping the window inside the 5.x major also preserves the original intent — the 1.x and 2.x instances under eslint/jest stay untouched rather than being force-marched across two breaking majors. npm's bundled copy (node_modules/npm/node_modules/brace-expansion) is unreachable by overrides and is carried by the `npm` pin instead.

js-yaml.reason: High-severity advisory (CVE-2026-59869) affecting js-yaml >=4.0.0 <4.3.0, reached transitively through cosmiconfig in the dev tree. Range-KEYED (`js-yaml@>=4.0.0 <4.3.0`) so it moves ONLY the vulnerable 4.x instance up to 4.3.0 and leaves the separate @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config 3.15.0 nested pin (js-yaml 3.x API) untouched. Added 2026-07-25.

sharp.reason: HIGH libvips CVEs (CVE-2026-33327/33328/35590/35591) inherited by sharp <0.35.0, pulled transitively via next@16. Pinned to an exact 0.35.3 — deliberately STRICTER than the 0.35.0 fix — in #1694 to clear the moderate+ npm-audit gate that had turned main red fleet-wide. patchedFrom records the upstream fix (0.35.0), not our floor; corrected from 0.35.3 on 2026-07-25 so the recorded fact matches the advisory.

valibot.reason: Moderate advisory pulled transitively through the production prisma / @prisma/dev chain. No direct dependency on valibot, so forcing the patched 1.x line through an override is the only lever. Added in #1698 alongside the js-yaml direct bump.

@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin.reason: Keeps every @typescript-eslint entry-point on one version. A split graph makes the parser and plugin disagree about AST shape.

@typescript-eslint/parser.reason: Paired with the plugin override above — same version, one AST contract.

typescript-eslint.reason: The umbrella package; pinned with its two constituents so flat config resolves one line.
